title: Sections of an invertible module over an affine open
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $M$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For an affine open $U\subseteq X$, put $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$ and $N=\Gamma(U,M)$. Then $N$ is an invertible $A$-module: the canonical evaluation map $\operatorname{Hom}_A(N,A)\otimes_A N\to A$, $\varphi\otimes n\mapsto\varphi(n)$, is bijective.

proof.text: An invertible sheaf is finite locally free, so its sections on U are finitely presented by finitePresentation_projective_sections. Refine each rank-one trivialization to a basic open D(g) in U. These g generate the unit ideal, and the basic-open localization theorem identifies the localization of N with the sections on D(g); the trivialization gives a linear equivalence with the coordinate ring. Module.Invertible.of_isLocalized_span then proves bijectivity of the evaluation map. This is the existing, sorry-free proof of invertible_sections_of_isAffineOpen in the cited source module; no new Lean theorem is stated.
